newsitem.title: SPAIN: RALLYING-MCRAE LEADS SUBARU OPENING DAY CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE LEADS SUBARU OPENING DAY CHARGE.

text.p: The Subaru team made up for their double retirement in Portugal three weeks ago as Briton Colin McRae and Italian Piero Liatti filled the two top positions after the first day of the Catalunya Rally on Monday.

The battling team mates, who finished one-two in this rally last year, were separated by just one second at the end of the day's six stages through the mountains above the coastal resort of Lloret de Mar.
"There have been almost no problems at all," said a Subaru spokeswoman. "In fact, the only drama was when Piero hit a stone on the first stage and suffered a puncture, which lost him a little time."
The real story of the day, however, was the surprising pace of the two-wheel drive Peugeot cars driven by Frenchmen Francois Delecour and Jules Pazzini, who had threatened to dominate the event.
Delecour took the lead on the first stage but after losing it to Pazzini on the second stage he went off the road on the third stage, at Coll de Santigosa, and dropped out of contention.

That handed the initiative to Pazzini who slowly extended his lead over early second-placed Fin Tommi Makinen in a Mitsubishi and then later McRae as the battle behind him hotted up during the middle section of the day.
But on the final stage, at Cladells, Pazzini lost a lot of time after suffering a puncture which effectively cost him any realistic chance of victory.
With McRae and Liatti fighting their own private battle at the front, reigning world champion Makinen was beginning to lose touch with the leaders, ending the day 11 seconds behind Liatti.

The most disappointed man was local hero Carlos Sainz who ended the day in fifth spot after suffering brake problems throughout the six stages with his Ford Escort. "We are not sure what they are, but they should be fixed by tomorrow," said a Ford spokesman.
Tuesday's second leg takes the teams south of the Lloret de Mar base towards Vinebre before once again returning to the coastal town in the late evening for an overnight halt.
